thread.title: Sonos Stock Falls On Greater-Than-Expected Loss, In-Line Sales

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Sonos Stock Falls On Greater-Than-Expected Loss, In-Line Sales
text:
Home sound system maker Sonos ( SONO ) late Monday reported a greater-than-expected loss and in-line sales for its fiscal third quarter ended June 30. Sonos stock fell in extended trading.
X The Santa Barbara, Calif.-based company lost 45 cents a share on sales of $208.4 million in the quarter. Analysts expected it to lose 22 cents on sales of $208 million. In the year-earlier period, Sonos lost 26 cents on sales of $223.1 million.
It was the first quarterly report from the consumer electronics firm since it went public on Aug. 2 at 15 a share. Sonos stock hit a record high of 23.60 on its second day of trading.
Sonos stock tumbled more than 12% in after-hours trading, near 18.85, on the stock market today . During the regular session, it soared 13.3% to 21.24.

In recent years, it has faced heightened competition from smart speakers from Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ), Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google and others. Amazon Echo, Apple HomePod and Google Home speakers combine personal voice assistants with audio speakers.
Sonos doesn't have its own voice assistant, but its speakers support Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant.
Sales Guidance Matches Views For the full fiscal year ending Sept. 29, Sonos expects revenue of $1.11 billion, based on the midpoint of its guidance. That's in line with Wall Street analyst estimates.
It did not give a target for earnings per share. Analysts have been modeling Sonos to lose 19 cents a share for the year.
Sonos hopes to deliver a compound annual revenue growth rate of at least 10% over the coming years, Chief Executive Patrick Spence said in a letter to shareholders . The company is targeting a compound annual growth rate of at least 20% for adjusted earnings, he said.
"We are focused on driving sustainable, profitable growth for the long term," he said. "We have grown our revenue for 12 consecutive years and scaled to nearly $1 billion in annual revenue with only approximately $110 million of primary capital raised since inception (pre-IPO). We've done this by being long-term-focused and responsible in how we invest."
Sonos Unit Sales Up, Revenue Down Sonos sold nearly 887,000 products in the third quarter, up 11% year over year. But despite the double-digit percentage increase in products sold, revenue declined 7%.
Wireless speakers accounted for 45% of the company's revenue in the quarter. Home theater speakers contributed 32% of revenue. The rest came from components and other items.
